A1.justification: Both PDFs describe INSEC, despite the changed title and organization. Text, equations, figures, tables, and v2's appendices A–G support reliable comparison; v1 has no separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original attack evaluations on four completion engines, vulnerability and functional-correctness measurements, ablations, and case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original results on StarCoder2, attack composition and transfer, repository completion, evaluation validation, and defenses.

M1.justification: The five initialization schemes and mutation–selection optimizer remain substantially unchanged. V2 Section 4.4 adds a composite attack that inserts separately optimized CWE strings on separate lines, extending v1's single-CWE procedure without redesigning its optimizer.

E1.justification: The original 16-CWE, five-language coverage is retained. V2 adds repository-context completion using RepoBench, human-written C++ and JavaScript reference solutions from HumanEval-X, and simultaneous targeting of multiple CWEs, substantially extending the evaluated data and scenarios.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates unattacked engines and internal attack variants but only discusses potential defenses. V2 Appendix F adds quantitative comparisons involving security-inducing comments, comment scrubbing, and Jain et al.'s perplexity filtering. This introduces a substantial defensive comparison component; it does not add a competing attack algorithm.

E3.justification: V2 adds StarCoder2 models at three sizes, a 333-instance RepoBench protocol using EM, ES and CodeBLEU ratios, sampled multi-CWE combinations, and defense-testing procedures. Reported attack lengths also change: v1 describes five tokens for StarCoder-3B and ten for the other engines, whereas v2 Appendix A specifies five generally, with Copilot-specific exceptions of ten or fifteen. This reporting revision does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds attack-composition and cross-model transfer analyses, a manual CodeQL precision audit, validation against human-written reference solutions, and experiments on security comments, comment removal, ASCII-only optimization, and perplexity defenses. The original position, initialization, tokenizer, length, temperature, and case-study analyses remain, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report aggregate point estimates without confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run and seed summaries. V2's additional sampled tasks and CWE combinations expand experimental design; they do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original four-engine results match between v1 Figure 2 and v2 Figure 3. V2 adds StarCoder2-3B/7B/15B results, with clean versus attacked vulnerability rates of 13%/62%, 21%/67%, and 29%/73%, respectively. Substantial additional results cover composition, transfer, RepoBench, HumanEval-X validation, 98% CodeQL precision on 50 audited instances, and defenses.

T1.justification: The vulnerability-rate, pass@k, and relative-functional-correctness definitions remain mathematically equivalent despite renaming and reordering. The adversarial-engine composition is restated, and neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs. V2's added low-overhead requirement is qualitative.

C1.justification: The central claim of practical black-box attacks that increase insecure completions while largely preserving functionality remains. V2 adds implemented IDE deployment as an explicit abstract contribution and changes the introduction's cross-engine increase from over 50 percentage points to around 50.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands interpretations of composability, transferability, attack-token patterns, and defenses' security–utility tradeoffs. Appendix F explains why accurate assessment of known CWEs does not establish static analysis as a general defense. The targeted-only limitation is superseded by composition experiments, while v1's explicit caveat about larger, more complex vulnerabilities is no longer retained.

D1.justification: V2 announces a public code and dataset release and adds model-version information, approximate GPU optimization time, rule-based vulnerability classifiers used during optimization, excluded mutation tokens, and VSCode deployment details with a code listing. These are substantial reproducibility disclosures, not evidence that every newly documented implementation choice changed.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against random-search jailbreaks, semantic-preserving code attacks, and concurrent RAG-context attacks, alongside additional defense and deployment literature. Section 6 now distinguishes these approaches through access requirements, per-query optimization, stealth, and preservation of functionality; these are substantive additions beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, threat model and method are consolidated into Section 3, and detailed algorithms, initialization explanations, experiments, and case studies move into appendices. Metrics are renamed, discussion and related work are reordered, and the title and author information change.

P2.justification: V2 adds an attack-flow diagram, deployment screenshots, and new experimental displays; expands the main results figure; and redraws initialization distributions from grouped bars into pie charts. It also merges temperature plots, changes plot scales and styling, relocates existing figures and algorithms, and adopts a different main-text and appendix layout.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical credibility and practical substantiation. Where v1 asserted CodeQL reliability and proposed IDE deployment, v2 provides a bounded precision audit, reference-solution validation, repository-context testing, and an implemented deployment demonstration. Defense experiments and reproducibility disclosures further improve assessability. Reporting ambiguities remain, including changed attack-length descriptions alongside unchanged original scores, and the deployment is not an end-to-end attack study; nevertheless, the added validation resolves important evidential gaps.
